title: 一念 · 萬物相連 — An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: Ink bloom and the first thought
scenes.purpose: Show diluted ink blooming into cool grey washi, then the brush writing 一 and the 今 component of 念 in stroke order.
visuals: Stationary cool blue-grey washi paper with seeded fibres and a soft vignette
Diffuse diluted-ink bloom behind the glyph area
一 (橫) then 念 strokes 丿, ㇏, 丶, ㇇ revealed along their centrelines
assets: index.html (procedural SVG brush strokes, no external images)

beats.development: The ink bloom forms where the character will appear, and 一 is written from left to right with a pressed start and a weighted end.
The 今 component of 念 is written in order: the left-falling stroke with a dry-brush split tail, then the right-falling stroke with a heavy foot, the dot, and the 橫撇.

scenes.title: Heart, seed and connections
scenes.purpose: Complete 心 (heart/mind) beneath 今, then let a seed dot branch into a connected ink network, with annotation columns, the seal and the caption arriving after the glyph.
visuals: 心 strokes 丶, ㇃ 臥鉤, 丶, 丶 in order
A second ink bloom on the left marks the network's origin
Tapered ink lines branch from the seed dot, and each node lands as its line arrives
Vertical columns 萬物相連 and 丙午秋 fade in
The vermilion seal (frame and carved 連 as one group) presses down

beats.development: 心 is written. As the 臥鉤 sweeps, a second bloom and the large seed dot appear on the left, and the main branch begins to draw.
captions: An idea becomes a connected system

beats.development: The branches extend, and each node appears when its line reaches it. 萬物相連 fades in top to bottom, followed by 丙午秋, and the seal stamps down.
captions: An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: Reading hold
scenes.purpose: Hold the completed composition so it can be read while the ink blooms continue to diffuse slowly.
visuals: The blooms are still slowly spreading and fading

beats.development: Everything is in place. Only the diluted ink blooms keep diffusing, so the frame does not look frozen.
captions: An idea becomes a connected system

findings: Brush strokes take 0.09–0.26 s each, scaled to stroke length and weight, with short brush lifts between them so the stroke order can be read.
The annotation columns and seal appear only after the glyph is complete, following the source-frame rhythm of building the glyph and then annotating it.
The English caption is fully opaque from 2.05 s, giving about 0.95 s of settled reading time for one short line within a 3 s preview.
justifiedHolds: 2.5–3.0 s: the closing reading hold, kept alive by the slow bloom diffusion rather than by new information.

notes: The stroke paths are hand-authored centrelines with pressure-width profiles. They follow standard stroke order, but they are not traced from a verified calligrapher's exemplar or a stroke-order database, because none is installed.

The cool grey washi background is a scene-dependent choice for a systems/technical subject, following the BACKGROUND_REVIEW background options. The ink #20211E and seal vermilion #B4382A are kept from the palette.
